301.author: wyhohyw
301.body:
Re-running a GitHub Actions job leaves the previous attempt's artifact in the same workflow run. `actions/download-artifact` resolves an exact name to one package, and that package can be the older attempt.

This showed up on PR #295, workflow run [38526631198](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38526631198). The first UT attempt failed one test and uploaded `ut-coverage` at 07:30 with manifest `status: FAIL` (3821 passed, 1 failed). UT was re-run and passed, uploading a second `ut-coverage` at 07:47. Coverage then ran with `needs.ut.result=success` but read the 07:30 package. `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` treats "the job passed, but the manifest is not PASS" as incomplete coverage and exits 1.

`upload-artifact@v4` does not replace an existing name unless `overwrite: true`. The same lookup applies to every artifact a later job downloads by exact name (`st-coverage`, `mocked-e2e-plan`, `real-e2e-plan`).

Coverage is not a required status check. `main` requires only `merge-gate`, which does not include Coverage, so this red job does not block merge. It does report the wrong run.

## Acceptance

- A successful re-run of UT replaces `ut-coverage`, so Coverage reads that attempt's manifest.
- The same replacement applies to the other artifacts a later job downloads by exact name.
- A contract test fails if a workflow downloads an artifact by exact name and the matching upload omits `overwrite: true`.
301.title: [Bug]: Re-running a job leaves Coverage reading the previous attempt's artifact

305.author: HongyeZhou
305.body:
## Motivation

Currently, every conversation must belong to a project, and creating a project requires too much configuration before users can start chatting.

This adds friction to the first interaction: users who simply want to ask a question or explore an idea must first create and configure a project, even when they do not yet need one. It also encourages creating projects for one-off conversations, making project management unnecessarily cluttered.

Users should be able to open the application and start a conversation immediately, then organize their work into projects when needed.

## Proposed direction for discussion

1. **Make project membership optional for conversations.**
   - Provide a prominent “New chat” entry that works without creating or selecting a project.
   - Support standalone conversations for quick questions, exploration, and one-off tasks.
   - Keep project-based conversations available for ongoing research and related work.

2. **Allow users to organize conversations into projects later.**
   - Let users move a standalone conversation into a new or existing project.
   - Preserve conversation history and associated artifacts when moving it.
   - Make it clear whether a conversation belongs to a project.

3. **Simplify project creation.**
   - Require only the minimum information needed to create a project, such as its name.
   - Provide sensible defaults and make advanced configuration optional.
   - Allow users to update project settings later instead of requiring them before the first conversation.

4. **Provide clear navigation for both workflows.**
   - Make standalone conversations and projects easy to find.
   - Let users start a conversation directly from the main interface.
   - Within a project, let users create conversations associated with that project.

## Example user flows

### Start chatting immediately

Open the application → New chat → Send a message.

No project creation or project configuration is required.

### Organize an exploratory conversation

Start a standalone conversation → Decide to continue the work → Move the conversation into a new or existing project.

### Start with a project

Create a project with minimal information → Start a conversation → Configure additional project settings when needed.

## Questions to settle

- Should standalone conversations remain in chat history by default, with an explicitly ephemeral mode handled separately?
- Which project settings can use defaults, and which are genuinely required before a project-specific capability runs?
- When an existing conversation moves into a project, how should project context and settings apply to subsequent messages?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user with no projects can open the application and send a first message without creating or configuring a project.
- [ ] Users can create and continue conversations outside projects.
- [ ] Users can still create conversations directly within a project.
- [ ] A standalone conversation can be moved into a new or existing project without losing its history or associated artifacts.
- [ ] Project creation requires only minimal information; advanced settings can be configured later.
- [ ] Navigation clearly distinguishes standalone conversations from project conversations.
- [ ] Existing projects and their conversations remain accessible.
- [ ] E2E coverage verifies starting a conversation with no projects, creating a project with minimal input, and moving a standalone conversation into a project.
305.title: [Feature]: Allow conversations outside projects and simplify project creation

307.author: zhaozhaozz
307.body:
## What is wrong

In Web settings, the free-engine group is titled:

- English: `Free search engines (tried after paid)`
- Chinese: `免费搜索引擎（付费之后尝试）`

The Chinese parenthetical reads as “try these only after you have paid.” A reader can think the free engines are locked until a paid plan is purchased. They are not. DuckDuckGo, Bing, and Brave’s public result pages need no API key and no paid provider. Search tries a keyed paid provider first when one is configured, then these engines. With no paid key, only the enabled free engines run.

The English parenthetical is the source of that translation. “Tried after paid” is also easy to read as “after payment,” rather than “after the keyed paid providers.”

The longer help text above the groups already states the real order. The group title contradicts that reading.

## Where

- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, key `webSettings.freeLegend` (both locales)
- Rendered by `apps/web/src/WebSettingsEditor.tsx` as the free-engine fieldset legend
- `apps/web/tests/WebSettingsEditor.test.tsx` asserts the current English legend and must change with it

Search order, provider keys, and which engines are requested stay as they are. `docs/zh/reference/web-tools.md` already describes the order and does not use this title.

## Suggested copy

Keep one fact in the title: these engines do not need a key. Keep the attempt order in the hint under the group, so it is not lost and is not phrased as a payment requirement.

- `webSettings.freeLegend`
  - English: `Free search engines (no API key)`
  - Chinese: `免费搜索引擎（无需密钥）`
- `webSettings.freeHint`
  - English: `No API key is required, and a paid provider is not required. Keyed paid providers are tried first; these engines are tried, in the order shown, only when those return no results. A switched-off engine is never requested.`
  - Chinese: `无需密钥，也不需要先开通付费服务。已保存密钥的付费服务商会先尝试；它们没有返回结果时，再按显示顺序尝试这里仍开启的引擎。已关闭的引擎不会被请求。`

A shorter title is fine if it cannot be read as “available only after payment,” and if the English and Chinese titles say the same thing.

## Acceptance

- The Chinese title no longer says `付费之后尝试`, and does not otherwise say that payment is required before these engines can be used.
- The English title no longer says `tried after paid`.
- The hint under the group still says that a switched-off engine is never requested, and that keyed paid providers are tried first when they are configured.
- The Web settings render test matches the new English title.
- No change to which engine is called, or to the paid-then-free attempt order.
307.title: [Bug]: Free search engines title reads as if payment is required

308.author: zhaozhaozz
308.body:
## What to change

On a large screen the Session conversation is too narrow, and it sits on the left. The composer under it is a different width. User messages should be a bubble on the right.

This is layout only. Do not change what a message contains, the right-hand artifact panel, or the narrow-screen stacking behavior.

## Current layout

The conversation pane is the left track of `.content-grid` (`apps/web/src/styles/conversation.css`). The right track is a fixed 390px panel.

Inside the conversation pane:

- Each `.message` and the run timeline are capped at `820px` and are not centered, so on a wide pane they stay on the left. The same `820px` cap is repeated for the message skeleton, process records, and several timeline blocks (`conversation.css`, `timeline.css`, `process-records.css`, `feedback.css`).
- The composer does not use that cap. It stretches across the pane with `margin: 0 max(28px, 5vw) 28px`, so on a large screen it is wider than the transcript above it.
- A user turn is the same left grid as an assistant turn: a 40px avatar column, then the body. `.message.user .markdown-body` is only an inline block with a sunk background. It is not on the right.

## What other agents do

Public pages do not publish a single official pixel width. The pattern that matches this request:

- **Doubao (doubao.com).** The transcript and the input share one centered column (`--center-content-max-width`, `--content-max-width`, `--chat-area-max-width` on the chat route). The column stays centered in the area beside the left navigation as the window grows; it is not the full window. User sends are a separate right-aligned bubble. Community style scripts refer to a stock send-message cap around `max-w-650`, and they right-align that bubble with `margin-left: auto`. The stock column is what people widen with userscripts; one width slider starts at 760px, another forces 1600px. Those overrides are “make it full width,” which is not what we want. A public recreation of the Doubao column uses `max-width: 1000px`.
- **WorkBuddy.** The published UI is a left task list, a center conversation, and an optional right results panel. The input sits at the bottom of that same center column, so the transcript and the input are one width. The docs do not give a pixel width or say which side a user message sits on.
- **Trae.** Side chat is the IDE panel on the right (Command+U / Ctrl+U). Its width is the panel the user drags, not a centered reading column. It is a poor template for this screen.

## Target

On a wide conversation pane, one centered column holds the transcript and the composer. Make it a little wider than 820px, and do not let it fill the pane.

Use **1000px** as the shared max width (`min(1000px, 100%)`, centered with `margin-inline: auto`). That is the modest step implied by “a little wider,” and it matches the 1000px Doubao-style column rather than the 1600px full-width userscripts. Put the number in one custom property and point the transcript, timeline, process records, skeleton, and composer at it, so the old `820px` copies cannot drift apart.

The composer’s outer width is that column. Its inner padding can stay. Short viewports keep today’s full-width behavior, including the ~900px case where the sidebar must not cover the conversation.

User messages, inside that column:

- The bubble sits on the right.
- A short message is only as wide as its text. A long message wraps and may use the column width, but it still starts from the right.
- Assistant replies stay on the left and use the column width.
- Do not leave the user avatar in the left gutter while the bubble is on the right. Keep the avatar with the bubble, or drop the user avatar if it fights the bubble. Assistant avatars stay on the left.

## Acceptance

- At a desktop width where the conversation pane is clearly wider than 1000px, the transcript and the composer are the same width, centered in the pane, and that width is 1000px rather than 820px or the full pane.
- A short user message is a bubble on the right of that column. An assistant message stays on the left.
- Below the width of the column, the column fills the pane and the composer still matches it. The existing narrow layout, including the sidebar at about 900px, still fits on the first screen.
- The right artifact panel stays 390px.
- A Web layout test or the existing conversation render test covers the shared column and the right-aligned user bubble.
308.title: [Feature]: Center a wider conversation column and right-align user bubbles

309.author: zhaozhaozz
309.body:
## What is wrong

On a large screen the artifact viewer is still a small card. It is the dialog opened from an artifact (`artifact-modal-panel` in `apps/web/src/styles/dialogs.css`):

- width `min(1080px, 100%)`
- only a max height, `calc(100vh - 56px)`, so a short file stays as short as its content

On a 1920px-wide window that width is about 56% of the viewport. On a 2560px window it is about 42%. Plots, tables, notebooks, and source previews then sit in a column that does not use the screen the user is looking at.

The same class is the shell for the evidence viewer and the node-detail viewer (`ScientificArtifacts.tsx`, `EvidenceModal.tsx`, `DetailModal.tsx`). They should grow with it. Confirmation dialogs and settings panels use other classes and stay small.

## What a reasonable size is

A decision dialog and a content viewer are different objects.

- Material’s dialog cap (560dp wide, 48dp from the screen edge) is for a question or a confirmation. Applying it here would make the viewer smaller.
- A content viewer should take most of the viewport and leave a visible margin, so the dimmed page and the click-outside close still read as a layer. A hard pixel cap still matters on a 4K display, or a paragraph becomes one very long line.
- WorkBuddy opens an artifact as a tab in the right-hand pane, and that pane can go fullscreen. This product’s right pane is 390px, which is too narrow to become the viewer. Growing the existing dialog is the change; do not move artifact viewing into that pane.
- This repo already treats specialized viewers as large windows: the CSV workspace is `min(1480px, 97vw)` by `min(920px, 95vh)` (`apps/web/src/csv-artifact/styles.css`), and the molecule window is `min(1360px, 96vw)` by `min(880px, 93vh)`. The generic artifact dialog is the one that did not follow that pattern.

## Target

On a wide screen, size the artifact viewer like those content windows, one step larger:

- width `min(1600px, calc(100vw - 80px))`
- height `min(960px, calc(100vh - 80px))`

That is 1600×960 when the window is large enough, and it shrinks with an 80px total margin when it is not. It does not go edge to edge. At `max-width: 900px` the existing rule already makes this panel full viewport; leave that rule alone.

Inside the window, prose stays readable. Markdown body copy keeps a measure of about 76ch. Tables, code, images, and plots use the window width. Do not widen a paragraph to 1600px.

The evidence title already ellipsizes at `min(560px, 60vw)`. That cap can stay. The comment above it still says the panel is about 1080px; update the comment if that block is touched.

## Out of scope

- Settings, creation, and deletion dialogs.
- The CSV workspace and the molecule window. They are already larger than 1080px.
- The 390px workspace panel.
- The conversation column width.

## Acceptance

- At a desktop width of about 1920px, the artifact viewer is 1600px wide and 960px tall, centered, with the page still visible around it.
- At a width between 900px and 1600px, the viewer is the viewport minus about 80px, not stuck at 1080px.
- At 900px and below, the viewer is still the full viewport, as it is today.
- A markdown artifact’s paragraphs do not run the full 1600px. A wide table or source preview does use the window.
- Evidence and node-detail viewers use the same size. A settings dialog does not.
- A render test, or a CSS assertion next to the existing dialog styles, locks the new width and height.
309.title: [Feature]: Make the artifact viewer use a large screen

310.author: HugoXK
310.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


`/evolve-design` is the only entry point for program evolution today, but it is a **hidden slash command** — a user must already know to type the `/evolve-design` prefix. The only visible entry is a button inside the artifact detail modal (it fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` and still requires the user to complete and send the sentence manually).

Two problems follow:

1. **We assume the user knows the command.** The UI never guides anyone toward `/evolve-design`; ordinary researchers will not type a slash command they have never seen.
2. **The interaction is command-shaped.** The user must learn command syntax (`--algorithm puct/openevolve`) instead of speaking naturally.

Goal: a user expresses improvement intent in **natural language** (e.g. "make this result better", "帮我优化这个程序"), the **framework actively recommends a tree-search evolution**, and the interaction stays natural-language end to end — no slash-command literacy required.



### Design Ideas

Land in three layers, reusing the existing `/evolve-design` chain (`EvolveAlgorithmPicker`, `EvolveToolRuntime`, `/api/evolve/runs`, the native-agent turn). No new capability surface.

#### Layer 1: Composer intent recognition (frontend, minimal)

Lightweight, testable, pure-function intent detection in the composer (no LLM round-trip):

- Match program-evolution intent:
  - the `/evolve-design` slash prefix (existing behavior, kept), **or**
  - a sentence pairing an **improvement verb** with an **evolvable target** (program / code / algorithm / function / model / script / …), in Chinese or English.
- When matched, offer a **low-intrusion suggestion bar** ("It looks like you want to improve a result or program. Run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") — the user must explicitly accept before anything is started.
- On accept, show the existing `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`; on select, fill `/evolve-design --algorithm X <natural language>` and send.

**Why confirmation before the picker?** Starting a search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations). Detection is a guess, so it must only *offer*; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This also protects against misreads — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never sent down an expensive search.

#### Layer 2: Agent-driven recommendation (backend, core value)

In the native-agent turn loop, recognise improvement intent in messages that do *not* carry the `/evolve-design` prefix:

- When the user asks to improve a program/result, the Agent **recommends** a tree-search evolution in its reply and offers to start it, reusing `EvolveToolRuntime`'s `create_evolve_run`.
- The interaction stays natural-language: the user replies "yes, go ahead", and the Agent starts the run.

#### Layer 3: Visible entry point (frontend, complete experience)

- A "program evolution" entry in the composer opens a **natural-language prompt** ("Which artifact? What does 'better' mean here?") instead of filling a slash command.
- The artifact-detail modal button opens the same prompt instead of generating `/evolve-design ...` text.

### Intent recognition rules

`detectEvolveIntent(message)` returns true only when **both** an improvement verb and an evolvable target are present, and no non-evolvable target is named:

| Example | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` | true | verb + program target |
| `make this better` / `把这个做得更好` | false | no explicit evolvable target |
| `optimize the interface layout` / `优化一下界面布局` | false | layout is not evolvable |
| `improve the workflow steps` | false | steps are not evolvable |
| `this result is better than the last one` / `这个更好` | false | no verb+target pair |
| `improve the description` / `改一下格式` | false | formatting/explanation excluded |

`isEvolveDesignCommand(message)` distinguishes the explicit command (goes straight to the picker) from natural language (goes through the suggestion bar).

### API surface

- No new public API; reuse `/api/evolve/runs` and `/api/evolve/runs/:id/events`.
- Layer 2 reuses `EvolveToolRuntime`'s existing tools; no new registration.
- Intent detection is a pure frontend function, unit-testable.

### Affected modules

- `apps/web/src/App.tsx`: composer intent detection; `showEvolveAlgorithmPicker` trigger extension (currently matches only the `/evolve-design` prefix); suggestion-bar state.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveSuggestionBar.tsx` (new): confirmation bar.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts` (new): `detectEvolveIntent` / `isEvolveDesignCommand`.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveAlgorithmPicker.tsx`: reused unchanged.
- `apps/web/src/api/evolve.ts`: reused.
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts`: turn-loop intent recognition and recommendation (Layer 2).
- `packages/evolve`: `EvolveToolRuntime` reused.
- i18n: suggestion-bar copy, composer entry copy (en + zh).

### Involved Public APIs

_No response_

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

_No response_

### Test Design and Test Plan

**Functional**

- [ ] Unit tests for `detectEvolveIntent`: Chinese/English verb+target, no-target messages, non-evolvable targets, negation phrases.
- [ ] Unit tests for `isEvolveDesignCommand`: command vs natural-language separation.
- [ ] Composer + natural-language improvement intent + artifact reference → suggestion bar appears.
- [ ] Accepting the suggestion → algorithm picker appears.
- [ ] Selecting an algorithm → `/evolve-design` evolution run starts.
- [ ] Ordinary messages (no intent) → nothing appears, normal conversation.
- [ ] Artifact modal button → opens natural-language prompt, not a filled command.

**Regression**

- [ ] Existing `/evolve-design` command path unchanged; explicit `--algorithm` no longer re-opens the picker.
- [ ] Existing evolve E2E / unit tests pass.

**User-perspective E2E**

- User expresses improvement intent naturally → framework recommends → natural-language confirm → evolution run starts.
- A message without improvement intent never triggers the evolution recommendation.

### Notes

- Follows the product direction: "the framework recommends tree search, but the interaction stays natural language."
- Layer 1 (frontend intent recognition + confirmation bar) can land as an independent MR first; Layer 2 (Agent-driven recommendation) depends on the turn-loop change and can follow.


### Additional Information

_No response_
310.title: [Feature]: Natural-language program evolution: turn /evolve-design from a hidden slash command into a framework-recommended, natural-language interaction

312.author: HongyeZhou
312.body:
### Problem

Users face two obstacles when downloading ScienceDiscovery:

1. **Release downloads are difficult to discover.** Installation packages are listed under **Assets** on the GitHub Releases page. When this section is collapsed, users may miss the downloads or struggle to find the package for their platform.
2. **The website installation page lacks a version selector and defaults to an outdated version.** Version 0.3 is available, but the installation page still defaults to 0.2. Users cannot select a release version directly on the page and may install an older version unintentionally.

### Proposed improvements

**GitHub Releases**

- Add a clearly visible download section to each release description, with direct links to installation packages.
- Label each download by operating system and architecture so users can identify the appropriate package without expanding Assets.

**Website installation page**

- Add a version selector so users can choose between available releases.
- Default to the latest stable release, currently 0.3.
- Keep download links and installation commands consistent with the selected version.
- Update the default version when a new stable release becomes available.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can find installation package links in the release description without expanding Assets.
- [ ] Download links clearly identify the supported operating system and architecture.
- [ ] The website installation page provides a version selector.
- [ ] The installation page defaults to the latest stable release.
- [ ] Download links and installation commands match the selected version.
- [ ] Publishing a new stable release updates the website’s default installation version.
312.title: [Bug]: Release downloads are hard to find and the website installation page defaults to an outdated version

313.author: HongyeZhou
313.body:
### Problem

After deploying ScienceDiscovery from source, users cannot reliably access the application by opening its local web address directly.

They must first find the `Open to sign in` URL in the deployment logs and open that specific link. Otherwise, the web page reports an error because the browser has not received the required local authentication information.

This behavior is difficult to discover and creates an unnecessary setup step:

- Users may not know that the startup logs contain a required sign-in link.
- The link can be missed among other service logs.
- Users may assume the deployment failed when opening the local address produces an error.
- The workflow is inconvenient for remote deployments, background processes, and users who no longer have the original terminal output.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy and start ScienceDiscovery from source.
2. Open the local ScienceDiscovery web address directly in a browser.
3. Observe that the application cannot be used successfully and reports an error.
4. Return to the deployment logs and locate the `Open to sign in` URL.
5. Open that URL and observe that the application then works.

### Expected behavior

After a successful source deployment, users should be able to open the advertised local web address directly and use ScienceDiscovery without copying a special sign-in link from the startup logs.

Local authentication should be initialized automatically or handled through the web interface while preserving the existing security boundary.

### Suggested improvement

Remove the requirement to retrieve the initial sign-in URL from deployment logs. For example, the application could automatically establish the local browser session, redirect users through the required local authentication flow, or provide an authentication setup page when they open the regular application URL.

The startup logs may continue to print a convenient URL, but opening that exact URL should not be required for normal use.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can access a newly started source deployment from its regular local web address.
- [ ] Users do not need to search the deployment logs for an `Open to sign in` link.
- [ ] Opening the regular address does not produce an authentication-related error during first use.
- [ ] The behavior works when the service runs in the background and the original terminal output is unavailable.
- [ ] Local access remains protected by the intended authentication mechanism.
- [ ] Documentation no longer instructs users to retrieve a required sign-in link from startup logs.
313.title: [Bug]: Source deployments require users to find and open a sign-in link from the startup logs

314.author: HongyeZhou
314.body:
### Problem

Automatically generated session titles occasionally contain literal `<think>` tags.

These tags appear as part of the visible title instead of a clean summary of the conversation. This makes session titles confusing and harder to scan.

The issue is intermittent; the exact trigger has not yet been identified.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a new session and send a message.
2. Wait for the session title to be automatically generated.
3. Check the generated title.
4. Occasionally, the title contains literal `<think>` tags.

### Actual behavior

The generated session title includes `<think>` markup.

### Expected behavior

Automatically generated session titles should contain only a concise, readable summary of the conversation, without reasoning tags or reasoning content.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Automatically generated titles never display `<think>` or `</think>` tags.
- [ ] Reasoning content enclosed by these tags is excluded from the title.
- [ ] If no usable title remains after filtering, the application retains a safe default title.
- [ ] Regression coverage includes title-generation responses containing reasoning tags.
314.title: [Bug]: Automatically generated session titles occasionally contain `<think>` tags

323.author: zy95-12
323.body:
## Summary
From an ease-of-use perspective, **review / citation verification should turn on and run automatically when the task needs it**, instead of finishing the research run and expecting the user to trigger a separate review pass.

## Observed behavior
On a basic literature-research run (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0):

- Session had `reviewMode: auto` and `semanticReviewEnabled: true`.
- Enabled skills for the run were only `literature-searcher`, `evidence-extractor`, and `report-writer` — **`citation-reviewer` was not in the enabled skill set**.
- Run completed with report artifacts, but event stream showed **no `review.*` events** and **no citation-reviewer / dedicated semantic-review pass**.
- The agent only did informal metadata cross-checks via `web_search` during synthesis.

So “review is configured on” did not mean “review verification actually ran as part of the same task.”

## Why this is a usability problem
Users reasonably expect that if review is enabled (or the task type clearly needs verification — e.g. literature survey with claims/citations), the product **runs verification inside the same workflow** and surfaces pass/fail or review findings with the deliverable.

Having to notice that review didn’t run and then start another trigger breaks the “set and forget” experience and makes trust in the report harder.

## Expected behavior
When review is enabled (`reviewMode: auto` / `semanticReviewEnabled: true`) **or** when the workflow produces citation-backed claims / literature artifacts:

1. Automatically include / invoke the appropriate review path (e.g. `citation-reviewer` or semantic review) **in the same run**.
2. Surface a clear review result (passed / issues found / skipped with reason) next to the main artifacts — not only after a manual second kick.
3. If review cannot run (skill missing, connectors unavailable, etc.), make that **visible in the UI/run status**, not silent completion.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
- Treat review as a **default post-synthesis gate** for literature / evidence workflows when settings say auto.
- Or auto-enable `citation-reviewer` (and any required review skills) when those settings are on, so skill selection can’t silently omit verification.
- Make “review ran vs skipped” an explicit run outcome field users can see without digging into events.

## Environment / repro sketch
- Product: ScienceDiscovery linux prepackaged binary 0.2.0
- Task: basic CRISPR / SCD literature research
- Settings observed: `reviewMode: auto`, `semanticReviewEnabled: true`
- Outcome: report artifacts produced; no dedicated review pass in the same run

## Labeling
Usability / enhancement — not claiming a hard functional bug in the settings schema, but a product gap between “review configured” and “review actually executed when needed.”
323.title: Usability: auto-run review verification when needed (don’t require a second user trigger)

324.author: zy95-12
324.body:
## Summary
When a literature / research task needs outbound network (PubMed, arXiv, skill scripts, etc.) and the sandbox blocks egress, the agent should **ask the user for network permission** (or guide them to grant Sandbox network allowlist access) rather than proceeding blocked and falling back without a clear permission request.

## Observed behavior
On a literature-research run (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0):

- Global `/api/sandbox-network-settings` was `mode: "none"` with empty `allowedDomains`.
- Skill scripts and direct HTTP inside the sandbox failed with DNS / network denial (`Temporary failure in name resolution` to NCBI / arXiv hosts).
- The run continued without a user-facing “please grant sandbox egress for these domains” step; retrieval degraded to `web_search` only.

## Why this is a usability problem
Users who enable PubMed/arXiv connectors or kick off a literature task reasonably expect the product to either:

1. already have the needed egress, or  
2. **prompt them once** to allow the required hosts / switch Sandbox network mode,

not silently hit fail-closed sandbox policy and produce a weaker report.

## Expected behavior
When the agent (or a skill/subagent) hits a sandbox egress block that is required for the current task:

1. Surface a clear permission / settings request to the user naming the needed domains (or Sandbox network mode change).
2. Pause or offer a retry path after the user grants access, instead of only recording failures in artifacts.
3. Prefer asking over silent degradation when the user’s prompt explicitly asked for PubMed/arXiv (or similar) retrieval.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
- Detect sandbox network denials that match known research hosts and open a UI affordance tied to **System configuration → Sandbox network** (domain-allowlist / mode).
- Or have the control plane preflight: if session has PubMed/arXiv enabled and sandbox mode is `none`, warn or solicit allowlist before the run starts.

## Environment / repro sketch
- Product: ScienceDiscovery linux prepackaged binary 0.2.0
- Settings: sandbox network `mode: none`
- Task: CRISPR / SCD literature research requesting PubMed and/or arXiv
- Outcome: DNS/network failures in sandbox; no user prompt to grant egress; fallback to web_search

## Related
See also the review auto-run usability gap (#323).
324.title: Usability: when sandbox egress blocks research, ask the user for network permission instead of silently failing

325.author: zy95-12
325.body:
## Summary

Enabling scientific connectors (`arxiv`, `pubmed`) on a Session persists `enabledConnectorIds`, and `/api/connectors` lists those sources, but the live agent tool set can still contain **no** `mcp__arxiv__*` / `mcp__pubmed__*` tools. Literature runs then fall back to `web_search` only. This breaks the documented contract that Session-enabled MCP sources become governed agent tools (control-plane MCP, outside the sandbox).

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0** local instance.
2. Session with `enabledConnectorIds: ["arxiv","pubmed"]` (and typically `web`).
3. Confirm `/api/connectors` returns arXiv/PubMed manifests (`enabledByDefault: false`, `requestedCapabilities: ["mcp"]`, NCBI/arXiv `networkHosts`).
4. Run a literature workflow that activates `literature-searcher` (or ask the main agent to search PubMed/arXiv via MCP).
5. Observe run events / agent reports: **no** literature MCP tool calls; agent/subagent states that no literature-search MCP tool is present; only `web_search` (and failed `web_fetch`) are used.

Observed on session `27148ad0…`, run `dad3a25d…`.

## Expected

- If a connector id is in the Session’s effective `enabledConnectorIds` and the MCP source is **ready**, the corresponding tools (`mcp__<sourceId>__<toolId>`, e.g. `mcp__pubmed__search`, `mcp__arxiv__search`) must appear in the agent/subagent tool set (native: deferred directory + promotion; JiuwenSwarm: promoted at start per docs).
- If the underlying MCP server/catalog is **unavailable** or **degraded**, enabling the connector must not look “on with tools”; the run/UI/agent should surface catalog status (or refuse the enablement path) instead of silently omitting tools while checkboxes stay enabled.

## Actual

Session JSON and connector catalog UI/API show arXiv/PubMed enabled/listed, but `createMcpWorkspaceTools` injects nothing for those sources when `McpSourceCatalog.getStatus(...).availableTools` is empty. The agent proceeds with an empty MCP tool list and no hard error tied to the enabled connectors.

## Code pointers

Injection chain (also documented in `docs/zh/developer-docs/science-connectors.md` §3):

1. **Session enablement** → `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` passes `enabledSourceIds: settingsSnapshot.enabledConnectorIds` into `createMcpWorkspaceTools` (after `filterEnabledMcpSources` for plugin master/per-connector switches).
2. **Catalog gate** → `packages/artifact-manager/src/mcp-workspace-tools.ts` (`createMcpWorkspaceTools`): keeps only tools in `catalog.getStatus(sourceId).availableTools`. Empty `availableTools` ⇒ no tools for that source.
3. **Why `availableTools` can be empty** → `packages/data-source/src/catalog.ts` (`statusFor` / `getStatus`):
   - Catalog never refreshed → status `unavailable`, `availableTools: []`, error *"MCP catalog has not been refreshed"*.
   - MCP server `biomed` missing/disabled/errored → same empty list (`transport.mcpServerId: "biomed"` in `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts`).
   - Remote `listTools` missing or schema-incompatible with local `mcpToolName` (e.g. `pubmed_search`, `arxiv_search`) → `degraded` / tool omitted.
4. **Startup soft-fail** → `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts`: `mcpCatalog.refresh().catch(...)` only warns; API keeps running with an empty/failed catalog while `/api/connectors` still lists manifests from the registry (no status). Status lives on `/api/mcp/sources` instead.
5. **Deferred visibility** (native) → `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` `createMcpTools` marks MCP tools `deferred: true`. That only applies to tools that survived step 2; it does not explain a completely empty MCP set.

Related but separate: skill scripts under `skills/literature-searcher/scripts/*` need `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXTERNAL_URLS_PATH` / `config/external-urls.json` in the sandbox; that does **not** replace MCP injection. Skill docs say to use session MCP tools and not bundled scripts for literature search.

## Impact

- Users believe PubMed/arXiv are connected; retrieval silently degrades to web snippets.
- `literature-searcher` cannot fulfill its MCP-first contract.
- Hard to debug without checking `/api/mcp/sources` status vs Session checkboxes.

## Suggested fix direction (non-prescriptive)

- Treat “enabled but catalog unavailable/degraded” as a first-class Session/run signal (surface status next to connector toggles; emit a run warning or block start when every enabled literature source has zero `availableTools`).
- Ensure bundled `biomed` stdio MCP from `extensions_config.json` is healthy before advertising connectors as usable.
- Optionally include catalog status in `/api/connectors` so the UI cannot show “enabled” without readiness.

## Labels

bug, needs triage
325.title: [Bug]: Session enabledConnectorIds (arxiv/pubmed) does not expose MCP tools to the agent

326.author: zy95-12
326.body:
## Summary

Product `web_fetch` on clearly public HTTPS URLs (e.g. `https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/...`, `https://export.arxiv.org/...`, Europe PMC) fails with `INVALID_INPUT` and the message **"local and private network URLs are not allowed"**. That string is produced by the control-plane SSRF guard when DNS resolution returns no addresses or any blocked address — so public hosts are being **misclassified** (or DNS failure is labeled as “private”), not correctly blocked as private SSRF targets.

This is **distinct** from Session MCP connector exposure ([#325](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/325)): `web_fetch` is the global Web capability (vendor fetch via Jina/Tavily/Exa), not the PubMed/arXiv MCP path.

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0**, Session with Web tools available (`web` connector / product `web_fetch`).
2. Agent calls `web_fetch` with a public literature URL, e.g.:
   - `https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/<pmid>/`
   - `https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?...`
   - Europe PMC article HTTPS URLs
3. Tool returns `INVALID_INPUT` with *"local and private network URLs are not allowed"* (and/or the same text in the attempt error).

Observed alongside literature run `dad3a25d…` (session `27148ad0…`) when MCP literature tools were also missing.

## Expected

- Public, globally routable HTTP(S) hostnames that resolve to public address space must pass `assertPublicUrl` and proceed to the configured fetch provider (default Jina Reader, etc.).
- DNS **failure** / unresolvable host must return a distinct, actionable error (e.g. host could not be resolved), **not** the private-network SSRF message.
- Loopback / RFC1918 / link-local / ULA / multicast rejection remains correct for true SSRF cases.

## Actual

Public literature URLs fail with the private-network message before (or instead of) a normal upstream fetch attempt.

## Code path (path is correct; classification / messaging is wrong)

Documented in `docs/en/reference/web-tools.md`:

```text
Agent web_fetch
  → packages/data-source/src/web/workspace-tools.ts (workspace binding)
  → packages/data-source/src/web/broker.ts  WebBroker.fetch
       - parses URL, requires http(s), no credentials
       - permission.requirePrivilege({ action: "host", resource: hostname })
  → NativeWebProviderClient.invoke (packages/data-source/src/web/native/index.ts)
       - await assertPublicUrl(input.request)   ← failure mapped to WebProviderError(..., "invalid-input")
  → fetchJina / fetchTavily / fetchExa (packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts)
       - outbound to vendor endpoints from config/external-urls.json (`web.jina_endpoints`, etc.)
```

SSRF guard: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts` → `assertPublicUrl`:

- Rejects non-http(s), credentials, `localhost`.
- Resolves hostname via `dns.promises.lookup(..., { all: true })`.
- Throws `PublicUrlError("local and private network URLs are not allowed")` when:
  - `addresses.length === 0` (**DNS failure / empty result — same message as private**), or
  - `addresses.some(isBlockedAddress)` (any resolved address in private/loopback/link-local/ULA/multicast/etc.).

Broker maps `invalid-input` → product `INVALID_INPUT` (`packages/data-source/src/web/broker.ts` `invocationError`).

## Why public URLs can hit this

Likely causes (environment + guard semantics):

1. **DNS lookup failed or returned no records** on the API/control-plane host → empty `addresses` → identical “private network” error (misleading).
2. **Over-strict multi-address policy**: if *any* A/AAAA record is blocked, the whole URL is rejected even when a public address also exists.
3. Broken/sinkhole DNS returning private/ULA for external names (true SSRF-style resolution — message would then be accurate, but operators still need clearer diagnostics).

**Not** the sandbox network allowlist (`SandboxNetworkSettings` / bubblewrap): product Web runs on the Node control plane and uses Web proxy settings / vendor endpoints. Connector `networkHosts` apply to MCP governance URL checks, not to `assertPublicUrl`.

## Impact

- Agents cannot open public paper landing pages / API URLs via `web_fetch` when DNS or classification fails, even though `web_search` may still work.
- Error text steers debugging toward “private network / SSRF” instead of DNS, proxy, or dual-stack resolution.

## Suggested fix direction (non-prescriptive)

- Split error messages: unresolvable vs non-public address vs localhost literal.
- Log resolved addresses (or failure reason) on the WebInvocation attempt for supportability.
- Revisit `addresses.some(isBlockedAddress)` vs requiring at least one public address / family policy.
- Add regression tests for: public hostname resolving to public IPv4; DNS empty; mixed public+ULA; literal `127.0.0.1`.

## Related

- [#325](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/325) — Session-enabled arXiv/PubMed MCP tools not injected (separate root cause; literature should prefer MCP, not `web_fetch`).

## Labels

bug, needs triage
326.title: [Bug]: web_fetch rejects public PubMed/arXiv URLs as "local and private network"

327.author: zy95-12
327.body:
## Summary
During a literature-research run, the session timeline stays visually frozen on parallel tool cards that only say **Tool is running…** / **Running** for several minutes. There is no incremental progress (queries tried, sources failed, papers found so far), so the product feels stuck even though the run is still working.

## Observed behavior
On a CRISPR / SCD literature demo (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, screen recording ~7 min raw):

- Two parallel `task` / tool-call cards stayed on `Tool is running…` with a spinner.
- Roughly **3+ minutes** of the recording had almost no visual change in the main pane.
- The only extra cue was a sidebar tooltip such as `PubMed search: CRISPR SCD clinical · running`, not a progress update in the task itself.
- The run eventually completed and wrote a report; it was not a hard freeze.

## Why this is a usability problem
Users cannot tell “still working” from “stuck”. A literature search that fans out to subagents needs staged status (started search, source unavailable, N records so far, synthesizing) instead of a single indefinite spinner.

## Expected behavior
While a tool or subagent is running:

1. Show a short, updating status in the task card (phase + last meaningful event), not only “Tool is running…”.
2. Prefer human-readable progress over raw subagent paths / token counters as the primary signal.
3. If a source fails (connector missing, network denied), surface that failure in the running card instead of waiting until the final report.

## Not the same as
- Connector tools silently omitted when enabled (#325) — that is a functional bug.
- Sandbox egress should ask for permission (#324) — different ask.
- Empty-state copy that mentions CSV/charts on a literature session — separate copy issue.

## Environment
- ScienceDiscovery linux prepackaged binary 0.2.0
- Task: short PubMed/arXiv literature survey
- Evidence: session screen recording; main pane static while tools report Running
327.title: Usability: long-running literature tasks show no incremental progress (only 'Tool is running…')

328.author: zy95-12
328.body:
## Summary
The empty-session intro copy is easy to mislead and adds little usability value. Prefer **removing the intro prompt** (or at least never showing CSV/chart guidance on a literature-oriented session) rather than polishing it.

## Observed behavior
On a literature demo session with `enabledConnectorIds = ["arxiv", "pubmed"]`, the empty session main pane showed:

- Eyebrow: `empty.sessionReady` (“Session workspace ready”)
- Title: `empty.investigate` (“What should we investigate?”)
- Body: `empty.sessionCsvHelp` — “Drop a CSV into the workspace, then ask the configured model to analyze it and create a chart.”

That copy steers users toward CSV analysis even when the session is clearly for literature research.

## Code pointer
`apps/web/src/App.tsx` (empty session intro) currently picks copy roughly as:

- if `pubmed` **and** `uniprot` are both enabled → `app.sessionIntroPrompt` (TP53 / cited evidence brief example)
- else → `empty.sessionCsvHelp` (CSV + chart)

Strings live in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` (`empty.sessionCsvHelp`, `app.sessionIntroPrompt`, etc.).

So enabling only PubMed/arXiv (a normal literature setup) still falls through to the CSV message. The alternate intro is gated on an odd `pubmed && uniprot` pair, which is easy to miss and not aligned with literature workflows.

## Product judgment
From a usage perspective, this intro has **limited value**. It is fine to have no example prompt, but it is **not fine to mislead**. Suggested direction: **delete the intro prompt / CSV empty help** (or replace with a neutral, non-prescriptive empty state), instead of investing in smarter prompt suggestions.

## Expected behavior
- Empty session should not push “drop a CSV / create a chart” unless the user is actually in a CSV/analysis context.
- Prefer no intro over a wrong intro.
- If any example remains, do not gate literature-friendly copy on `pubmed && uniprot`.

## Priority
**Low** — polish / copy cleanup; not a blocker for core runs.

## Related
Not the same as long-running progress (#327) or connector MCP exposure bug (#325).
328.title: Usability (low): remove misleading empty-session CSV intro; don’t gate literature copy on pubmed+uniprot

330.author: zy95-12
330.body:
## Summary
During a literature-research run, the session **timeline is too engineering-oriented**. Parallel tool cards, subagent workspace paths, and token/turn counters dominate the main pane, so a researcher cannot quickly see *what is happening for the research task*. Progress that does exist is buried (e.g. a sidebar tooltip like `PubMed search: CRISPR SCD clinical · running`) while the main area stays on a large **INPUT** dump.

## Observed behavior
On a CRISPR / SCD literature demo (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, ~7 min raw screen recording):

- Two parallel `task` / tool-call cards filled the timeline with long specialist prompts (INPUT), UUIDs / `subagents/…` paths, model name, turn counts, and token usage.
- Primary status was often just `Running` / `Tool is running…`.
- The more human-readable status (`PubMed search … · running`) appeared mainly as a **sidebar hover tooltip**, not as the main-pane headline.
- Researchers scanning the UI struggled to answer: which searcher is doing what, what failed, how many papers so far, when synthesis starts.

## Why this is a serious usability problem
This is a research workbench UX issue, not mere polish:

1. Cognitive load: engineering telemetry (paths, tokens, raw INPUT) competes with the research narrative.
2. Progress opacity: meaningful status is secondary (tooltip / deep in cards) while the main column looks like a developer console.
3. Trust: when retrieval degrades (no MCP tools, sandbox/network failures), the timeline does not make the failure mode obvious at a glance.

Related but distinct from #327 (no incremental progress at all). Here the problem is **information hierarchy / audience**: even when something is updating, the wrong details are foregrounded.

## Expected behavior
For literature / research sessions (and ideally by default for non-debug users):

1. Timeline cards should lead with a **human-readable phase** (e.g. “Searching PubMed for clinical CRISPR/SCD papers”, “Source unavailable”, “Synthesizing 5 papers”).
2. Keep subagent paths, full INPUT blobs, token/turn stats behind an expand/debug control — not the default above-the-fold view.
3. Surface parallel branches as short labeled lanes (clinical vs mechanism) rather than two giant opaque tool cards.
4. Put the same status that today only appears in the sidebar tooltip into the main timeline card header.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
- Default “Researcher” timeline vs optional “Developer / debug” density.
- Collapse tool INPUT by default; show a one-line summary + live status.
- Promote connector/search failures into the card status line as soon as they happen.

## Priority
**High among usability issues** for research users (serious scanability / trust problem), though not a functional crash.

## Related
- #327 — long runs only show `Tool is running…` (progress missing)
- #325 — connectors enabled but MCP tools omitted (functional bug that makes the opaque timeline worse)
- #324 — sandbox egress should ask for permission
330.title: Usability: session timeline is too engineering-heavy for researchers (tool cards, subagent paths, tokens)

332.author: zy95-12
332.body:
## Summary

Docs describe adding a **custom MCP server**, but ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0** has no settings surface for it and the documented HTTP routes return **404**. End-to-end custom MCP cannot be demoed on this binary.

## Repro

1. Local ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 (`http://127.0.0.1:4310`).
2. Open **System configuration**. Groups present include Global defaults, Sandbox network, Network proxies, Skills, Specialists, Permissions, Connection, etc.
3. There is **no** “MCP servers / Custom / Add server” item. Bundle strings have no `mcp/servers`, `Add server`, or `Custom MCP`.
4. **Network proxies** only lists bundled sources (`biomed`, `uniprot`) and **Add proxy server** — not an MCP server.
5. Authenticated API:
   - `GET /api/mcp/servers` → `HTTP 404` `{"error":"Not found"}`
   - `POST /api/mcp/servers` (trivial stdio body) → `HTTP 404` `{"error":"Not found"}`
6. Contrast: `GET /api/mcp/sources` returns the 12 bundled connectors (all `unavailable` with empty `availableTools` on this instance — separate readiness bug, see #325).

Docs that claim the feature: [Configure custom MCP](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/docs/advanced-setup/configure-custom-mcp.html).

Observed during Scenario 2 Case C (project **自定义扩展演示**), recorded 2026-10-15.

## Expected

- Either ship a working custom-MCP settings page + `/api/mcp/servers` CRUD matching the docs, **or**
- Document that custom MCP is not in 0.2.0 and hide/relabel the docs until it ships.

## Actual

UI and API for user-added MCP servers are absent (404). Users following the docs hit a dead end.

## Priority

**High** among functional gaps for “custom extension” journeys — blocks the whole Case C path.

## Related

- #325 — Session-enabled bundled connectors do not expose MCP tools (catalog/readiness)
- Distinct from proxy policy under Network proxies
332.title: [Bug]: Custom MCP servers undocumented gap — UI missing and /api/mcp/servers returns 404

333.author: zy95-12
333.body:
## Summary

Uploading a PDF through the workspace **Drop files** control does not go through the paper-reader pipeline. Paper reader stays at **0 parsed**, and the agent only sees a raw file (often with almost no extractable scientific content unless it scrapes bytes itself).

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, new session in a data-analysis project.
2. Drop `experiment_notes.pdf` (+ optional CSV) via **Drop files**.
3. Ask the agent to read the PDF notes and fit kinetics from the CSV (no network).
4. Observe: Paper reader counter remains **0 parsed**. Agent reports extracting only the single plain line from the PDF and explicitly notes missing protocol/units/replicates. Units come from the CSV header, not from structured paper parse.

Observed Scenario 1 Case B (session `c6372af5-…`, project **数据分析演示**), 2026-10-15.

## Expected

- Dropping a PDF into the workspace should either:
  - enqueue it for paper-reader parsing (same as the dedicated paper input), **or**
  - clearly label the upload as “file only / not paper-parsed” so users do not assume literature extraction ran.
- If Drop files is intentionally file-only, the empty/paper UI should not imply paper intake for that artifact.

## Actual

PDF is a workspace file only. Paper reader stays **0 parsed**. Structured literature extraction does not run on Drop-files PDFs.

## Priority

**Medium–High** for any “upload paper + analyze” flow; easy to misread as a successful paper ingest.

## Related

Not the same as empty-session CSV intro (#328). Speaks to intake path consistency between Drop files and paper-reader.
333.title: [Bug]: PDF uploaded via Drop files is not parsed by Paper reader (0 parsed)

334.author: zy95-12
334.body:
## Summary

With the **Memory graph** disabled, the agent still attempts (or is expected to use) `declare_claim`, but claims cannot be recorded. The model falls back to saying so in chat instead of writing durable claims. That is a broken / half-wired tool surface rather than a clean capability gate.

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 with Memory graph off (default or global setting on this instance).
2. Run a data-analysis session that finishes with findings (Scenario 1 Case B: enzyme kinetics fit).
3. Observe run: model states that `declare_claim` could not record claims because memory graph is disabled; continues without faking citations.

Session `c6372af5-…`, project **数据分析演示**, 2026-10-15.

## Expected

One of:

1. When Memory is off, **do not expose** `declare_claim` (and related claim tools) in the agent tool set; or
2. Expose the tools but return a **structured, user-visible** “Memory disabled — enable in Settings” failure that the UI surfaces, not a silent omit / prose apology; or
3. Keep Memory on by default for research sessions so claim capture works out of the box.

## Actual

Claim recording is unavailable; the agent narrates the limitation. Users get neither claims nor a clear settings affordance tied to the failed tool.

## Priority

**Medium** — does not block analysis artifacts, but breaks the claim / evidence graph contract whenever Memory is off.

## Related

Timeline opacity (#330) makes this failure even harder to notice.
334.title: [Bug]: declare_claim fails / cannot record claims when Memory graph is disabled

335.author: zy95-12
335.body:
## Summary

In multi-step science demos, the agent repeatedly hits **tool-call failures** that it then recovers from on retry. Tasks still complete, but the timeline fills with failed cards and wasted turns. Two concrete patterns showed up in Scenario 2/3.

## Repro / observations

### A. Specialist `task` missing required prompt (Scenario 2 Case B)

1. Create custom specialist **CSV质检专员** bound to skill `csv-quality-check`.
2. Start a session with that specialist selected; upload CSV; ask for a quality check **without** naming the skill.
3. Parent `read_skill` completes; first `task` **fails** (missing required prompt field); retry **completes** with `specialistId` and skill path.
4. Subagent eventually COMPLETED; parent re-checks and declares artifacts.

Session `378644b7-…`, project **自定义扩展演示**.

### B. lmfit `conf_interval` signature (Scenario 3 Case A)

1. Domain-allowlist sandbox; `environment_create` task env; `environment_install` lmfit **1.3.4** from PyPI.
2. Fit Michaelis–Menten; two `run_python` calls **fail** on lmfit 1.3.4 `conf_interval` calling convention; later calls succeed after the agent fixes the call.
3. Final fit OK (Vmax/Km/R²), but timeline shows two failed Python cards.

Session `ae359b61-…`, project **科学计算演示**, 2026-10-16.

Similar soft failures also appeared in Scenario 1 (`run_shell` / `run_python` fail-then-complete).

## Expected

- Specialist delegation: first `task` payload should always include required fields (prompt) when the product launches a specialist subagent — schema/validation before the card is shown as failed.
- Scientific library helpers: either pin known-good call patterns in skills/examples, or catch common `conf_interval` / API mismatches with a clearer error that steers the next call without two opaque failures.
- Prefer failing closed in the UI with a one-line “retrying with fixed args” rather than raw failed tool cards as the default narrative.

## Actual

Runs complete via model self-repair, but users see multiple **failed** tool cards and longer wall time for routine fits / specialist handoffs.

## Priority

**Medium** — reliability / polish of the tool loop; not a hard blocker when Always-allow is on.

## Related

- #330 — engineering-heavy timeline makes these failures more alarming than they are
- #327 — long runs already lack incremental progress
335.title: [Bug]: Agent tool calls fail then recover mid-run (task missing prompt; lmfit conf_interval signature)

336.author: zy95-12
336.body:
## Summary

Every new session defaults to **Ask for dangerous actions**, even inside a project where the user already set **Always allow** on prior sessions. There is no project- or global-level default, so demos and repeated analysis require toggling the composer control every time.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 local demos (Scenarios 1–3, 2026-10-15/16):

- New project opens an Untitled session with approval = Ask.
- User must flip the composer control to **Always allow** (`aria-pressed=true`) before tools run smoothly.
- Creating another session in the same project resets to Ask again — not inherited from the sibling session or project.

Affects projects **数据分析演示**, **自定义扩展演示**, **科学计算演示**.

## Why it hurts

For trusted local sandboxes and scripted demos, re-confirming every session adds friction and invites accidental runs still on Ask (more interrupt cards) or forgetting to tighten back later.

## Expected

- Remember last choice per project, **or**
- Offer a project/global default (Ask / Always allow) that new sessions inherit, with a clear per-session override.

## Priority

**Medium** usability — repeated friction, not a functional blocker.

## Related

Distinct from sandbox egress solicitation (#324).
336.title: Usability: approval mode resets to Ask on every new session (no project-level default)

337.author: zy95-12
337.body:
## Summary

On first paint after opening the app, the sidebar can show **Projects 0** even when projects already exist, and the **Add project** button appears clickable but does nothing until global settings have finished loading. A later click opens Create Project. Easy to read as “broken UI”.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 (`http://127.0.0.1:4310`), Scenarios 1–2:

1. Open app (Local API already connected).
2. Sidebar briefly / initially shows **Projects 0** while a catalog project (e.g. 文献调研演示) already exists.
3. Click **Add project** once → no dialog.
4. After settings load, a later click opens **Create Project**.

Same pattern noted again when starting Scenario 2.

## Expected

- Disable or show a loading state on **Add project** until settings/catalog are ready.
- Do not render **Projects 0** when the catalog already has entries (show skeleton / previous count / spinner).
- Prefer one click → dialog once ready, never a silent no-op.

## Priority

**Medium** — first-run / return-user trust issue.

## Related

May share root causes with settings-load races tracked elsewhere (e.g. #290 / #291 family); this issue is the **user-visible Add project / Projects count** symptom.
337.title: Usability: Add project does nothing until settings finish loading; sidebar briefly shows Projects 0

338.author: zy95-12
338.body:
## Summary

Creating a project always drops the user into an auto-created **Untitled** session. The only rename path is the inline “Rename Session” field. Every demo (S1–S3) started with a rename before the real prompt.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0:

- **Add project** → project created → session titled Untitled.
- User renames in place (e.g. to Iris CSV 统计分析, Skill csv-quality-check, lmfit 酶动力学拟合).
- No prompt at project-create time for an initial session name; no sensible default from the project name.

## Expected (non-prescriptive)

- At Create Project, optionally ask for first session name; or
- Default the first session to the project name / “Session 1”; or
- Open rename focused automatically with clear placeholder copy.

## Priority

**Low–Medium** polish — small repeated friction on every new project.

## Related

Pairs with approval reset on new sessions (companion usability issue filed in the same demo pass).
338.title: Usability: new projects land on an Untitled session that must be renamed in place

339.author: zy95-12
339.body:
## Summary

System configuration → Skills → Import offers **Folder**, but the desktop/file control only accepts a **file path**. Choosing a skill package directory is rejected. Importing a lone `SKILL.md` works, which is fine for docs-only packages and **drops** `scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` for richer packages.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, Scenario 2 Case A (2026-10-15):

1. Skills → Import → Folder.
2. `setInputFiles` / file control on directory `/workspace/.../fixtures/csv-quality-check/` → rejected (directories not accepted).
3. Importing `/workspace/.../fixtures/csv-quality-check/SKILL.md` succeeded → Managed · r1 `csv-quality-check`.
4. That fixture had no scripts; a package with scripts would be incomplete via SKILL.md-only import.

UI also lists ZIP and Git repository (not exercised in this pass).

## Expected

- Folder import should accept a directory and preserve the full package layout, **or**
- If the browser/host cannot do directories, disable/hide Folder and steer users to ZIP / Git with clear copy.
- Do not advertise Folder if the control can only take a file.

## Priority

**Medium** for authors shipping skills with scripts/references.

## Related

Custom MCP absence is separate ([Bug] custom MCP /api/mcp/servers 404 — filed in the same pass).
339.title: Usability: Skill “Import folder” rejects directories — only a single file path is accepted

340.author: zy95-12
340.body:
## Summary

The workspace **Artifacts** list appears **project-scoped**: while working in session B, files from session A in the same project still show up (sometimes grouped under the other session’s name). Not a data-loss bug — the model still read the correct uploads — but the list is noisy and easy to mis-click.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 demos:

- Scenario 1: session B’s file count included session A artifacts.
- Scenario 2: during Specialist session, Case A reports still listed under “Skill csv-quality-check” while new files appeared under “Specialist CSV质检”.

## Why this may be intentional

Project-level sharing can be desirable (reuse a CSV across sessions, compare outputs). This issue is filed **low priority** to force an explicit product decision, not to demand an immediate change.

## Design questions (need a call)

1. Should Artifacts default to **current session only**, with an opt-in “Show project files”?
2. Or keep project scope but visually separate **This session** vs **Other sessions** with clearer hierarchy?
3. Should uploads be session-private by default and only promoted to project library on pin/share?

## Expected after a design pass

Whatever the choice, the panel should make scope obvious so users do not think another session’s outputs belong to the active run.

## Priority

**Low** — polish / information architecture; confirm against intended project-workspace model before changing.

## Related

Not a substitute for timeline density (#330).
340.title: Usability (low): workspace Artifacts panel is project-scoped and mixes other sessions’ files
